content: The Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (commonly known as the Alliance) has been accused of inciting subversion. Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, who pleaded not guilty, went through a 24-day trial and faced the verdict on Friday, August 21. Former vice-chairwoman Chow Hang-tung represented herself as a barrister to fight this case. In prison, without a computer or internet access, she handwritten hundreds of pages of submissions page by page. At her request, the court played in its entirety footage from two years of June 4th candlelight vigils, recreating the candlelight in Victoria Park point by point, as well as testimony from June 4th eyewitnesses. "So I am the last defendant, and also the last vice-chairperson of the first defendant, the Alliance... I am now 41 years old, a barrister, and there really isn't much else of a simple background to speak of," Chow Hang-tung said with a smile at the outset. During her six days of testimony, she smiled from time to time, but also broke down in tears several times. What do the June 4th vigils and the call to end one-party dictatorship mean to Chow Hang-tung? What was her "intention"? This episode of the Podcast continues to take readers to the courtroom, using a dramatised reading to recreate Chow Hang-tung's testimony, as well as the cross-examination by the judge and the prosecution.
